audit.why: 54.55% over 341 games against a chart that gives Camille levels 1 through 6 outright and turns both item stages into Skill. That is exactly the shape of a lane you win before stacks exist and lose if it goes long, and the mirror file audits/top/nasus__camille.json splits the stages the same way, so the two directions agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait it or trade only when it is on cooldown' is the core instruction of the lane and Wither's cooldown is never given. No Nasus cooldown appears anywhere.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s, Siphoning Strike 7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5/3.5s, Spirit Fire a flat 12s, Fury of the Sands 120/100/80s. The 15s on Wither at rank 1 is the entire trade window this matchup is built around.
audit.corrected: early, mid, whys[3] and wants.foe[0] now carry Wither's 15s so the bait-and-commit rule has a clock.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (1) The late game credits Fury of the Sands with 'bonus HP plus lifesteal'. Riot's text for his R gives bonus Health, increased ATTACK RANGE, an aura, and a shorter Siphoning Strike cooldown - the lifesteal is Soul Eater (P), which is on all game. That matters because it means the sustain you are fighting is not gated behind his ult. (2) Spirit Fire's armour shred is mentioned once in wants.foe but never connected to the fact that your Q recast is TRUE damage and ignores it entirely - which is why the recast, not the autos, is what you lean on when he shreds you. Camille's passive is spelled 'Adaptive Defense'; it is Adaptive Defenses. Hookshot is called a stun; Riot says knock-up, and the mirror file corrected the same wording from his side.
audit.why: Riot, Fury of the Sands: 'gains increased Health, Attack Range, damages nearby enemies, has a reduced cooldown on Siphoning Strike.' Soul Eater: 'Nasus drains his foe's spiritual energy, giving him bonus Life Steal.' Spirit Fire: 'dealing damage and reducing the Armor of enemies who stand on it.'
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text, late and whys[6] move the lifesteal onto Soul Eater and name the ult's real effects; early names the passive correctly and every Hookshot 'stun' becomes a knock-up.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds call, against a champion whose lifesteal is a permanent passive and is named as the reason you lose the late duel.
audit.why: Soul Eater is on from level 1 and Fury of the Sands only widens the gap; the mirror file bought Bramble Vest from his side for the same reason in reverse.
audit.corrected: late now names anti-heal against Soul Eater before the two-item stage.

edits.before: Once Nasus hits ~200+ Q stacks with Sheen and Spirit Visage, Wither cancels your attack-speed DPS and his R's bonus HP and lifesteal out-drain your W heal — the duel flips to him.
edits.after: Once Nasus hits ~200+ Q stacks with Sheen and Spirit Visage, Wither cancels your attack-speed DPS and Fury of the Sands adds bulk and reach over Soul Eater lifesteal — the duel flips to him.

edits.after: Wither you the instant you E in to gut your attack speed and movement, then walk out clean for the next 15s

edits.after: Pre-stack Nasus cannot punish your dives; bait Wither, then all-in during the 15s it is down.

edits.before: He out-scales hard: ~200+ Q stacks plus Wither neuter your attack-speed DPS and his R bulk and lifesteal out-drain you, so end before full build.
edits.after: He out-scales hard: ~200+ Q stacks plus Wither neuter your attack-speed DPS while Soul Eater lifesteal and R bulk out-drain you, so end before full build.

edits.before: Nasus is a free lane at Levels 1-3 — he has no Q stacks yet and no way to punish you, so deny his Siphoning Strike last-hits and zone him off the cannon wave. Respect Wither, though: the instant you E in, he can slow your movement AND attack speed to a crawl and walk out, so bait it or trade only when it is on cooldown. Your Q-recast true damage and Adaptive Defense shield mean you win the short exchanges he is forced into.

Respect Wither: the instant you E in he can slow your movement AND attack speed to a crawl and walk out, so bait it and commit inside the 15s it is down. Your Q-recast true damage and Adaptive Defenses shield win the short exchanges he is forced into.

edits.before: This is your takeover window. At 6 your Hextech Ultimatum locks Nasus in the arena where his one escape tool — Withering you and running — does nothing, and you delete him before he stacks. Keep punishing: E-Q-W chunks him for max HP, and every cs you deny is Siphoning Strike damage he never gets. Roam off your tempo lead while he is stuck farming under tower.
edits.after: This is your takeover window. At 6 your Hextech Ultimatum locks Nasus in the arena where his one escape tool — Withering you and running — does nothing, and you delete him before he stacks. Keep punishing: E-Q-W chunks him for max HP, and every cs you deny is Siphoning Strike damage he never gets. Spirit Fire shreds armour, so lean on the Q recast — true damage ignores it. Roam off your lead.

edits.before: If the game drags, Nasus reclaims it hard. Once he has ~200+ Q stacks, Sheen, and Spirit Visage, Wither shuts off your attack-speed DPS mid-dive and his R's bonus HP plus lifesteal out-drain your W heal — you cannot 1v1 him at full build. Close on your first-item lead, splitpush him off the map with your E mobility, and never let a fed Nasus catch you in melee range with Wither up.
edits.after: If the game drags, Nasus reclaims it hard. Buy Grievous Wounds early, close on your first-item lead, splitpush him off the map with your E mobility, and never let him catch you in Wither range.

edits.before: Good trade: Lead with the W outer edge as Nasus steps to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your bonus move speed before the fight goes long. Great trade: Nasus uses or whiffs Wither: instantly E off a wall for the stun and attack-speed surge, Q-recast for the true-damage second hit, W to heal, and R to isolate him if he tries to run. Bad trade: Burning Hookshot (E) aggressively, missing the stun, and getting stuck in a drawn-out melee grind while your E and shield are down. That is how Camille loses a winning lane.

notes: MIRROR REUSE: audits/top/nasus__camille.json already established from his side that Hookshot knocks up rather than stuns, that only the OUTER half of Tactical Sweep slows/heals, and that this pairing needs anti-heal - I kept all three consistent from Camille's side rather than re-deriving them. The find on my side is that the late game credits Fury of the Sands with lifesteal it does not have: the lifesteal is Soul Eater, a passive that is live from level 1, so a player waiting for his ult to start respecting his sustain waits too long. NOT ASSERTED: spikes[1].text claims The Hextech Ultimatum leaves him 'no Flash escape'. Nothing in either kit file settles whether Flash leaves the anchored area, and the mirror explicitly declined to confirm or remove the same claim, so I left it standing untouched and logged it as unverified rather than reinforce it.
